title: Fat Bear Week Is Back — and This Year It's Bigger Than Ever!
summary:
Imagine a bear that weighs more than a small car. That's Chunk — a brown bear in Alaska who won last year's Fat Bear Week contest. He weighs over 1,200 pounds!

Fat Bear Week is a fun online tournament. It happens every year in Katmai National Park and Preserve. The bears there eat lots of salmon from the Brooks River to get ready for winter. During winter, they hibernate — that means they sleep for months without eating. So they need to store up fat.

This year's bracket came out on Friday. It has 16 bears, up from 12 in recent years. That's more bears than ever before! Park Superintendent Mark Sturm said, "There are more cubs at Brooks Camp this year than have been seen in a long time." In fact, 37 cubs were counted at Brooks River.

You can vote for your favorite bear starting Tuesday, September 22. Voting takes a break over the weekend. The winner is announced on September 29. You can watch the bears on live webcams from Explore.org.

Some bears have cool nicknames. There's Bear 89, called "Backpack," because he had to ride on his mom's back after an injury when he was a cub. There's also Bear 151, known as "Walker," one of the most dominant bears on the river.

Last year's winner, Chunk, had a broken jaw but still ate a lot. He even played with younger bears. Will he win again? You can help decide!
why_it_matters: Fat Bear Week shows how animals get ready for a hard season, and it reminds kids that wild animals need clean rivers and enough fish if they are going to survive.

background_read: Katmai National Park and Preserve (a huge wild park in Alaska, the U.S. state farthest north) is famous for its brown bears and its volcanoes.
Every summer, many salmon swim up the Brooks River (a river inside the park) to lay their eggs, and the bears stand in the water to catch them.
Fat Bear Week started in 2014 as a fun way to teach people about bears; fans vote online, and the website Explore.org (which runs live animal cameras) lets people watch the bears all day long.
Article_Structure: WHO: Brown bears at Katmai National Park, including last year's winner Chunk and Park Superintendent Mark Sturm
WHAT: The yearly Fat Bear Week online voting contest, which has a bigger bracket this year with 16 bears instead of 12
WHERE: Katmai National Park and Preserve in Alaska, along the Brooks River
WHY: The bears must eat lots of salmon and store fat so they can hibernate through the winter

perspectives.description: They love watching the live webcams and voting, and they are happy that more bears and more cubs than usual are in the contest this year.
They say the contest is really a science lesson: it teaches people how hibernation works and why the river and salmon must be protected.
Some say it is just an internet popularity contest and the bears do not care who wins — the part that truly matters is keeping their wild home safe.
